context.title: Solomon's Court and Wisdom
context.summary: Solomon organizes his officials and twelve supply districts. His kingdom is large and peaceful, and his wisdom becomes famous across the region.
context.background: Each district supplied the royal household for one month a year (v. 7), and the districts did not simply follow the old tribal lines. 'The river' in v. 21 is the Euphrates, the far edge of Solomon's influence.

customs.note: The 'measure' here is the kor, the same size as a homer — a large dry measure traditionally linked to a donkey-load.

customs.term: Under his vine and fig tree
customs.note: A proverbial picture of peace and security: every family safely enjoying its own land.

watchFor: The promise to Abraham echoes in 'as the sand which is by the sea in multitude' (v. 20).
Solomon's wisdom includes nature study — trees, animals, birds, fish (v. 33).

people.name: Solomon
people.summary: Peaceful, (Heb. Shelomoh), David’s second son by Bathsheba, i.e., the first after their legal marriage (2 Sam. 12). He was probably born about B.C. 1035 (1 Chr. 22:5; 29:1).

people.name: Zadok
people.summary: A son of Ahitub, of the line of Eleazer (2 Sam. 8:17; 1 Chr. 24:3), high priest in the time of David (2 Sam. 20:25) and Solomon (1 Kings 4:4).

people.name: Azariah
people.summary: Son of Zadok—the priest.

people.name: Jehoshaphat
people.summary: Son of Ahilud, “recorder” or annalist under David and Solomon (2 Sam. 8:16), a state officer of high rank, chancellor or vizier of the kingdom.

people.name: Shavsha
people.summary: (“Seraiah,” 2 Sam. 8:17; “Shisha,” 1 Kings 4:3), one of David’s secretaries (1 Chr. 18:16).

people.name: Ahiah
people.summary: One of Solomon’s secretaries (1 Kings 4:3).

people.name: Abiathar
people.summary: Father of abundance, or my father excels, the son of Ahimelech the high priest. He was the tenth high priest, and the fourth in descent from Eli.

people.name: Benaiah
people.summary: The son of Jehoiada, chief priest (1 Chr. 27:5). He was set by David over his body-guard of Cherethites and Pelethites (2 Sam. 8:18; 1 Kings 1:32; 1 Chr. 18:17).

people.name: Jehoiada
people.summary: The father of Benaiah, who was one of David’s chief warriors (2 Sam. 8:18; 20:23).

people.name: Nathan
people.summary: A prophet in the reigns of David and Solomon (2 Chr. 9:29). He is first spoken of in connection with the arrangements David made for the building of the temple (2 Sam. 7:2, 3, 17), and next appears as the reprover of David on account of his sin with Bathsheba (12:1-14).

people.name: Azariah
people.summary: Son of Nathan.

people.name: Zabud
people.summary: Gift, the son of Nathan, who was “king’s friend” in the court of Solomon (1 Kings 4:5).

people.name: Adoniram
people.summary: One who was “over the tribute;” i.e., “over the levy.” He was stoned by the Israelites after they had revolted from Rehoboam (2 Chr. 10:18).

people.name: Abda
people.summary: The father of Adoniram, whom Solomon set over the tribute (1 Kings 4:6); i.e., the forced labour (R.V., “levy”).

people.name: Ahishar
people.summary: Brother of song = singer, the officer who was “over the household” of Solomon (1 Kings 4:6).

people.name: Ephraim
people.summary: Double fruitfulness (“for God had made him fruitful in the land of his affliction”). The second son of Joseph, born in Egypt (Gen. 41:52; 46:20).

people.name: Hur
people.summary: The Governor.

people.name: Abinadab
people.summary: One of Solomon’s officers, who “provided victuals for the king and his household.”

people.name: Baana
people.summary: One of Solomon’s purveyors (1 Kings 4:12).

people.name: Manasseh
people.summary: The elder of the two sons of Joseph. He and his brother Ephraim were afterwards adopted by Jacob as his own sons (48:1).

people.name: Jair
people.summary: Was the son of Segub of the tribe of Judah – Segub being a son of Hezron who married a daughter of Machir.

people.name: Geber
people.summary: Son of Uri—in Gilead.

people.name: Ahinadab
people.summary: Brother of liberality = liberal, one of the twelve commissariat officers appointed by Solomon in so many districts of his kingdom to raise supplies by monthly rotation for his household.

people.name: Iddo
people.summary: Timely.

people.name: Naphtali
people.summary: My wrestling, the fifth son of Jacob. His mother was Bilhah, Rachel’s handmaid (Gen. 30:8). When Jacob went down into Egypt, Naphtali had four sons (Gen. 46:24).

people.name: Ahimaaz
people.summary: Daughter of Solomon.

people.name: Asher
people.summary: Happy, Jacob’s eigth son; his mother was Zilpah, Leah’s handmaid (Gen. 30:13). Of the tribe founded by him nothing is recorded beyond its holding a place in the list of the tribes (35:26; 46:17; Ex. 1:4, etc.) It increased in numbers twenty-nine percent, during the thirty-eight years’ wanderings.

people.name: Hushai
people.summary: Quick, “the Archite,” “the king’s friend” (1 Chr. 27:33). When David fled from Jerusalem, on account of the rebellion of Absalom, and had reached the summit of Olivet, he there met Hushai, whom he sent back to Jerusalem for the purpose of counteracting the influence of Ahithophel, who had joined the ranks of Absalom (2 Sam. 15:32, 37; 16:16-18).

people.name: Baanah
people.summary: Son of Hushai, another of Solomon’s purveyors (1 Kings 4:16).

people.name: Issachar
people.summary: Hired (Gen. 30:18). “God hath given me,” said Leah, “my hire (Heb. sekhari)...and she called his name Issachar.” He was Jacob’s ninth son, and was born in Padan-aram (comp. 28:2).

people.name: Jehoshaphat
people.summary: Solomon’s purveyor in Issachar (1 Kings 4:17).

people.name: Paruah
people.summary: Flourishing, the father of Jehoshaphat, appointed to provide monthly supplies for Solomon from the tribe of Issachar (1 Kings 4:17).

people.name: Benjamin
people.summary: The younger son of Jacob by Rachel (Gen. 35:18). His birth took place at Ephrath, on the road between Bethel and Bethlehem, at a short distance from the latter place.

people.name: Shimei
people.summary: One of David’s mighty men who refused to acknowledge Adonijah as David’s successor (1 Kings 1:8).

people.name: Elah
people.summary: One of the dukes of Edom, Shimei ben-Elah was Solomons commissariat officer in Benjamin.

people.name: Sihon
people.summary: Striking down. The whole country on the east of Jordan, from the Arnon to the Jabbok, was possessed by the Amorites, whose king, Sihon, refused to permit the Israelites to pass through his territory, and put his army in array against them.

people.name: Og
people.summary: Gigantic, the king of Bashan, who was defeated by Moses in a pitched battle at Edrei, and was slain along with his sons (Deut. 1:4), and whose kingdom was given to the tribes of Reuben and Gad and half the tribe of Manasseh (Num. 21:32-35; Deut. 3:1-13).

people.name: Geber
people.summary: A valiant man, (1 Kings 4:19), one of Solomon’s purveyors, having jurisdiction over a part of Gilead, comprising all the kingdom of Sihon and part of the kingdom of Og (Deut. 2; 31).

people.name: Uri
people.summary: Father of Geber.

people.name: Judah
people.summary: Praise, the fourth son of Jacob by Leah.

people.name: Dan
people.summary: The fifth son of Jacob. His mother was Bilhah, Rachel’s maid (Gen. 30:6, “God hath judged me”, Heb. dananni).

people.name: Darda
people.summary: Pearl of wisdom, one of the four who were noted for their wisdom, but whom Solomon excelled (1 Kings 4:31).

people.name: Ethan
people.summary: “The Ezrahite,” distinguished for his wisdom (1 Kings 4:31). He is named as the author of the 89th Psalm.

people.name: Heman
people.summary: 1 Kings 4:31; 1 Chr. 2:6, a son of Zerah, noted for his wisdom.

people.name: Mahol
people.summary: Dance, the father of four sons (1 Kings 4:31) who were inferior in wisdom only to Solomon.

places.name: Israel
places.summary: Kingdom, -1094 to -974 (1Sam.10.1 to 2Chr.10.19); added from Digital Manna places-1255 (LPF sync 2026-10-13)

places.name: Beth-shemesh
places.summary: A sacerdotal city in the tribe of Dan (Josh. 21:16; 1 Sam. 6:15), on the north border of Judah (Josh. 15:10). It was the scene of an encounter between Jehoash, king of Israel, and Amaziah, king of Judah, in which the latter was made prisoner (2 Kings 14:11, 13).

places.name: Shaalbim
places.summary: now Salbit

places.name: Abel-meholah
places.summary: Meadow of dancing, or the dancing-meadow, the birth-place and residence of the prophet Elisha, not far from Beth-shean (1 Kings 4:12), in the tribe of Issachar, near where the Wady el-Maleh emerges into the valley of the Jordan, “the rich meadow-land which extends about 4 miles south of Beth-shean; moist and luxuriant.”

places.name: Beth-shean
places.summary: House of security or rest, a city which belonged to Manasseh (1 Chr. 7:29), on the west of Jordan. The bodies of Saul and his sons were fastened to its walls.

places.name: Jezreel
places.summary: A town of Issachar (Josh. 19:18), where the kings of Israel often resided (1 Kings 18:45; 21:1; 2 Kings 9:30). Here Elijah met Ahab, Jehu, and Bidkar; and here Jehu executed his dreadful commission against the house of Ahab (2 Kings 9:14-37; 10:1-11).

places.name: Jokmeam
places.summary: Gathering of the people, a city of Ephraim, which was given with its suburbs to the Levites (1 Chr. 6:68).

places.name: Megiddo
places.summary: Place of troops, originally one of the royal cities of the Canaanites (Josh. 12:21), belonged to the tribe of Manasseh (Judg. 1:27), but does not seem to have been fully occupied by the Israelites till the time of Solomon (1 Kings 4:12; 9:15).

places.name: Taanach
places.summary: A sandy place, an ancient royal city of the Canaanites, on the south-western border of the plain of Esdraelon, 4 miles south of Megiddo. Its king was conquered by Joshua (12:21).

places.name: Zarethan
places.summary: When the Hebrews crossed the Jordan, as soon as the feet of the priests were dipped in the water, the flow of the stream was arrested. The point of arrest was the “city of Adam beside Zaretan,” probably near Succoth, at the mouth of the Jabbok, some 30 miles up the river from where the people were encamped.

places.name: Argob
places.summary: Stony heap, an “island,” as it has been called, of rock about 30 miles by 20, rising 20 or 30 feet above the table-land of Bashan; a region of crags and chasms wild and rugged in the extreme.

places.name: Bashan
places.summary: Light soil, first mentioned in Gen. 14:5, where it is said that Chedorlaomer and his confederates “smote the Rephaim in Ashteroth,” where Og the king of Bashan had his residence.

places.name: Gilead
places.summary: Hill of testimony, (Gen. 31:21), a mountainous region east of Jordan. From its mountainous character it is called “the mount of Gilead” (Gen. 31:25).

places.name: Ramoth-gilead
places.summary: Heights of Gilead, a city of refuge on the east of Jordan; called “Ramoth in Gilead” (Deut. 4:43; Josh. 20:8; 21:38). Here Ahab, who joined Jehoshaphat in an endeavour to rescue it from the hands of the king of Syria, was mortally wounded (1 Kings 22:1-36).

places.name: Mahanaim
places.summary: Two camps, a place near the Jabbok, beyond Jordan, where Jacob was met by the “angels of God,” and where he divided his retinue into “two hosts” on his return from Padan-aram (Gen. 32:2).

places.name: Naphtali
places.summary: Added from Digital Manna places-1260 (LPF sync 2026-10-13)

places.name: Asher
places.summary: Added from Digital Manna places-1264 (LPF sync 2026-10-13)

places.name: Bealoth
places.summary: Citizens, a town in the extreme south of Judah (Josh. 15:24); probably the same as Baalath-beer (19:8).

places.name: Issachar
places.summary: Added from Digital Manna places-1265 (LPF sync 2026-10-13)

places.name: Egypt
places.summary: The land of the Nile and the pyramids, the oldest kingdom of which we have any record, holds a place of great significance in Scripture.

places.name: Euphrates
places.summary: Hebrew, Perath; Assyrian, Purat; Persian cuneiform, Ufratush, whence Greek Euphrates, meaning “sweet water.” The Assyrian name means “the stream,” or “the great stream.”

places.name: Gaza
places.summary: Called also Azzah, which is its Hebrew name (Deut. 2:23; 1 Kings 4:24; Jer. 25:20), strong, a city on the Mediterranean shore, remarkable for its early importance as the chief centre of a great commercial traffic with Egypt.

places.name: Tiphsah
places.summary: Passing over; ford, one of the boundaries of Solomon’s dominions (1 Kings 4:24), probably “Thapsacus, a great and wealthy town on the western bank of the Euphrates,” about 100 miles north-east of Tadmor.

places.name: Beersheba
places.summary: Well of the oath, or well of seven, a well dug by Abraham, and so named because he and Abimelech here entered into a compact (Gen. 21:31). On re-opening it, Isaac gave it the same name (Gen. 26:31-33).

places.name: Dan
places.summary: The fifth son of Jacob. His mother was Bilhah, Rachel’s maid (Gen. 30:6, “God hath judged me”, Heb. dananni).

places.name: Lebanon
places.summary: White, “the white mountain of Syria,” is the loftiest and most celebrated mountain range in Syria. It is a branch running southward from the Caucasus, and at its lower end forking into two parallel ranges, the eastern or Anti-Lebanon, and the western or Lebanon proper.

events.title: Reign of Solomon
events.summary: Passage: 1 Kings 2:12–11:42. People: Solomon. Place: Jerusalem. Lasted about 40 years.
